title: Cooking Food
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Every cooking practical is done with the teacher at the fire or stove. Children stand back from hot oil; long sleeves are rolled up and hair tied back.

skills.key_step: The child describes boiling (in bubbling water), steaming (over steam, not in the water), roasting (in dry heat over fire or in ashes) and shallow frying (in a little hot oil, turned once).

floor.prerequisite: Knows heat is used to cook.
floor.question: Name a use of heat at home.

representations: a chart: method, what cooks the food
a demonstration of steaming bananas over water
steps: Steaming: food above the water, in the steam.
Roasting: dry heat, no water or oil.
Shallow frying: a little hot oil.

board.do: Draw a pot of water with a basket of food above it.

misconceptions.ask: In steaming, where is the food?
misconceptions.repair: Show a steamer with the food on a rack above the water.

listen_for: A pot full of oil to cover the food
misconceptions.ask: What is used in shallow frying?
misconceptions.repair: Show a frying pan with a spoonful of oil beside a pot full of oil.

listen_for: In a pot of boiling water
misconceptions.ask: How is a maize cob roasted?
misconceptions.repair: Roast a cob over a jiko and compare it with a boiled cob.

listen_for: Nothing, boiling is only for water
misconceptions.repair: Show an egg going into a pan of boiling water and coming out cooked.

checks.question: How is roasted maize cooked?
checks.answer: in dry heat over a fire

checks.question: How much oil is used for shallow frying?

skills.key_step: The child picks a method that suits the food (green vegetables quickly, beans and maize boiled long, eggs boiled or fried) and says how to tell it is cooked well.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the four methods of cooking.
floor.question: What is steaming?

representations: a chart: food, best method, time
pictures of well and badly cooked vegetables
steps: Name the food: hard or soft?

board.do: Ask which needs the longer cooking.
Write "hard foods long, green vegetables short".

misconceptions.ask: Which method suits dry beans best?
misconceptions.repair: Try to fry dry beans and ask why they stay hard.

listen_for: For a very long time until it is soft and brown
misconceptions.ask: How long should sukuma wiki be cooked?
misconceptions.repair: Cook greens for 3 minutes and for 30 minutes and compare colour and taste.

misconceptions.ask: Which food needs the longest time to cook?
misconceptions.repair: Put beans and spinach in two pots and see which is soft first.

misconceptions.ask: Why cook sukuma wiki quickly instead of boiling it for an hour?
misconceptions.repair: Compare bright green quickly cooked sukuma with grey overcooked sukuma; ask which looks and tastes better.

checks.question: Which takes longer to cook: dry beans or cabbage?
Give a food cooked by shallow frying.

skills.key_step: The child says how to cook safely (turn pot handles in, stay with the fire, use a dry cloth to hold hot pots, cover a burning pan, never use water on an oil fire, keep children away) and to clean up at once.

floor.question: Can hot water burn the skin?

representations: a picture of a stove with handles turned in and out
a dry cloth and a lid
steps: Hold hot pots with a dry cloth.
Clean pots and surfaces straight away.

board.do: Draw a pan with a handle sticking out over the edge.
Ask what could happen when a small child walks past.
Wait for "it could be knocked and burn them".
Turn the handle in on the drawing.

listen_for: Sticking out, so it is easy to reach
misconceptions.ask: How should the handle of a pot on the stove be turned?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens when a child passes and brushes the handle.

misconceptions.ask: The oil in a pan catches fire. What should be done?
misconceptions.repair: Talk about why water makes burning oil splash and spread.

listen_for: Go out and play, it will be fine
misconceptions.ask: The pot is on the fire. What should the cook do?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what can happen to a pot that boils dry or a fire that spreads.

misconceptions.ask: When should the pots and surfaces be cleaned after cooking?
misconceptions.repair: Leave a crumb of food on a plate overnight in a jar; look at the flies or mould the next day.

checks.question: What do you put on a small pan of burning oil?
checks.answer: a lid or a damp cloth, never water

checks.question: Why turn pot handles in?
checks.answer: so nobody knocks the pot over
